title: Ruby
subtitle: A language designed for programmer happiness, where everything is an object and blocks make code read like prose, from a first script to idiomatic, tested, professional Ruby.
description: Ruby is a dynamic, object-oriented programming language created in Japan by Yukihiro "Matz" Matsumoto and first released in 1995. Its stated aim is to make programmers productive and happy: everything in Ruby is an object, blocks let you pass behaviour to methods as naturally as you pass values, and the standard library is rich and consistent. Ruby is best known for Ruby on Rails, the web framework behind many well-known web applications and countless smaller ones, and it is also used for command-line tools, automation, infrastructure software and data processing.

This course is for anyone who already knows what a variable, a loop and a function are: the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience in any language. It begins with Ruby's philosophy and your first scripts, works through objects, control flow, methods and blocks, collections and the Enumerable module, classes and mixins, metaprogramming, pattern matching and error handling, and ends with concurrency (threads, fibers and Ractors), gems, Bundler and testing, an overview of Rails, and a complete small project.

To run the code, install Ruby by following the official guide at [ruby-lang.org](https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/documentation/installation/) (a version manager such as rbenv or mise on macOS and Linux, RubyInstaller on Windows), or use the official Docker image `ruby`. You can also try Ruby in the browser at [TryRuby](https://try.ruby-lang.org/). Every complete program in these lessons was run with Ruby 4.0 by Lumenary's test suite, and the output shown is the output it printed. The lessons were drafted with AI assistance and are awaiting review by a human computer scientist.

levels.title: Foundations
levels.summary: Install Ruby and meet its philosophy, then learn the core language: objects, numbers, strings and symbols, control flow, methods, blocks, procs and lambdas, and the collections that Enumerable makes so expressive.

levels.title: Practice
levels.summary: Design with classes, modules and mixins, bend the language with metaprogramming (and know when not to), and handle data and failure with pattern matching and exceptions.

levels.title: Professional
levels.summary: Do several things at once with threads, fibers and Ractors, and work the way Ruby teams do: gems, Bundler, Minitest, RuboCop, an overview of Rails, and a complete project.
